## Hi, I'm Richa!

::: {.text-center}
![](images/headshot.jpg){width=250}
:::

I’m a graduate student studying analytics at Boston University with a background in cognitive science and computer science. My interests have always been a mix of understanding people, working with technology, and figuring out how information can be used to solve problems. That combination is what ultimately drew me toward analytics.

Through school and my professional experience, I’ve had the opportunity to work with real datasets across several industries, including EV charging and energy infrastructure, HVAC and building technology, sales, logistics and delivery operations, hospitality and short-term rentals, and the job market. These experiences have exposed me to different types of data and business problems, from analyzing sales and operational performance to exploring customer and market trends. I’ve found that I especially enjoy working through large or messy datasets, figuring out which patterns actually matter, and using what I find to answer practical business questions and support better decisions.

## My Interests

What interests me most about analytics is the combination of technical and human problem-solving. Because of my background in cognitive science and computer science, I’m interested in both how technology works and how people interact with it. I’m especially curious about customer behavior, product strategy, emerging technologies, and how organizations can use data to make better decisions.

Outside of purely technical analysis, I also enjoy thinking about how products and processes can be designed more effectively for the people using them. I like work that gives me the opportunity to ask questions, explore different perspectives, and understand the reasoning behind the numbers rather than only focusing on the numbers themselves.

## Career Goals

My goal is to build a career in data analytics and business intelligence, where I can work on problems involving operational performance, customer and market trends, forecasting, and business strategy. I’m especially interested in roles where I can use tools like SQL, Python, Power BI, and Excel while also working closely with business teams to understand their needs and help guide decisions.

As I gain experience, I’d like to take on more ownership of analytics projects from start to finish—from defining the problem and analyzing the data to presenting recommendations to stakeholders. Long term, I hope to grow into a position where I can lead analytics initiatives and help shape broader business and technology strategy.
